USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Withdrawal counseling

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A parent reports that a child has been free of absence seizures for several months on ethosuximide. The parent plans to stop the medicine tomorrow without consulting the neurology team. Which counseling point is most appropriate?

  1. Seizure freedom proves the underlying epilepsy is cured
  2. Take all remaining capsules on the last day
  3. Switch to intermittent doses only on school days
  4. Replace ethosuximide with an over-the-counter antihistamine
  5. Do not stop abruptly; arrange a supervised withdrawal plan if appropriate
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Do not stop abruptly; arrange a supervised withdrawal plan if appropriate

Abrupt antiseizure-drug withdrawal can precipitate seizures, including absence status.

Understanding the options

Do not stop abruptly; arrange a supervised withdrawal plan if appropriate
Abrupt antiseizure-drug withdrawal can precipitate seizures, including absence status.
Seizure freedom proves the underlying epilepsy is cured
Control during treatment does not establish cure.
Take all remaining capsules on the last day
This risks overdose rather than safe withdrawal.
Switch to intermittent doses only on school days
Irregular dosing can destabilize seizure control.
Replace ethosuximide with an over-the-counter antihistamine
Antihistamines do not substitute for epilepsy therapy.
